user_questions.question: (1) RenderGiftCardAction and the IssueGiftCardAction duplicate guard only look up certificates with Status__c = 'Active'. Once the automation moves a certificate to Partially Redeemed, the agent can no longer find it. Options: (a) leave those classes unchanged (recommended; not asked for), (b) also update them to include Partially Redeemed. (2) Status__c is hand-editable and has Draft, Expired, and Cancelled values. Should the automation override those? Options: (a) never override Cancelled, Expired, or Draft (recommended), (b) override any status based on remaining value, (c) never override only Cancelled and Expired.
user_questions.simulated_answer: (1) No preference; use your recommended default. (2) Never override Cancelled/Expired/Draft.

skill_friction: RUNNER says to use validate_spec.py with --root, which SKILL.md step 8 does not mention; works but the two documents disagree on the save path (design/ vs out).

spec-format.md says to add a FlowTest row 'only when it can assert the flow's main outcome', but gives no guidance on how many FlowTest components to add when a flow has several outcomes (each FlowTest holds one trigger scenario), or on the FlowTest API name convention; I chose three FlowTests and guessed the names and folder (force-app/main/default/flowtests).

Step 5 lists 'automation that overwrites values people edit by hand' as an ask trigger, but the requirement itself asks for exactly that; unclear whether the protected-status question was required or should have been decided from the picklist semantics.

Reverse transitions (remaining restored to original) are not covered by the requirement; Rule 4 says drop unrequested behavior while spec-format asks to cover records that start/stop matching. Kept it as an assumption; the skill does not say which rule wins.
AskCoworker kept citing 'prior session' and a 'bounds validation rule (separate requirement)' despite the ignore-earlier-conversations header; handled via the drop rule.
